items.d: Marinated beef cooked in a domed pan with vegetables and its own liquid. This is the bulgogi most people outside Korea have met.
Beef finely chopped, shaped into patties and grilled. A different answer to the same problem of thin, tender beef over fire.

items.t: Gwangyang style — slices on a mesh grill
items.d: Paper-thin beef laid on a mesh grill over live charcoal, no broth and no pan. The Korea Herald reported in 2022 that Gwangyang houses season the meat the same day rather than marinating it ahead, and that a slice is turned within about 30 seconds.

slides.title:
A regional dish
with a return
address
slides.body:
Most regional Korean specialties dissolve into folklore when you look for a starting point. This one has an address you can still walk to.

The house opened in 1930 as Ilheung Sikdang. The record, as summarised on Wikipedia from Gwangyang News, has the second generation developing the grilled dish the place became known for and renaming it Gwangyang Bulgogi Sikdang; the third generation gave it the name it carries today. Neighbouring restaurants took up the method until it was the food the whole city is identified with.

Gwangyang does have an older story — maro-hwajeok, a handed-down phrase naming the grilled beef of Maro, the Baekje-era name for the area, as the finest thing under heaven. That is legend, not record. What is documented is the fuel: oak charcoal from Baegunsan, the mountain behind the city.

Gwangyang bulgogi is named after a city — but the version the city is known for was worked out in one kitchen.

Samdae Gwangyang Bulgogijip · 52 Seocheon 1-gil, Gwangyang · open since 1930, now in its fourth generation.
